newsitem.title: USA: Clinton defense fund says not target of DOJ probe.
newsitem.headline: Clinton defense fund says not target of DOJ probe.

text.p: President Clinton's legal defense fund is not the target of a Justice Department investigation into possible improper donations to the president's campaign, a top official said Sunday.

"We have been advised that the trust is not a target nor the subject of the investigation which is limited to the campaign financing," Michael Cardozo, executive director of the defense fund said on ABC Television's "This Week" program.
On Thursday, the Presidential Legal Expenses Trust said it had received a subpoena from the Justice Department concerning contributions collected by Charles Yan Lin Trie, an Arkansas restauranteur.
A Justice Department task force investigating the campaign contributions has also subpoenaed the White House and the Democratic National Committee.
Cardozo said the defense fund would cooperate with the investigation. "We will cooperate and promptly respond," he said. The defense fund has had no contact with the DNC, he added.
On Monday, the trust fund announced that it had given back $640,000 in contributions raised by Trie, who has known Clinton for 20 years, saying it viewed them as "questionable."

The fund began investigating the donations virtually as soon as they were received, Cardozo said. "We immediately initiated a screening process that was in place," he said. Once the investigation concluded the donations might be improper, the donations were returned.
Clinton, under fire for Democratic Party fundraising tactics during the election, has said he was unaware Trie had been raising most of the money in question until it came in.
Cardozo also defended a meeting he had with first lady Hillary Clinton two weeks after Trie made the donations.

"The purpose of the meeting with Mrs Clinton was to determine if she could give us any guidance as to who Mr. Trie was," Cardozo said. Once Mrs Clinton was told an investigation had begun, "she supported that and asked us to be extremely vigilant," Cardozo said.
Republicans continued to attack the donations.

"What we have here are blatant violations of existing laws," Sen. Mitch McConnell, R-Ky., chairman of the Senate Ethics Committee said on the ABC program. "I just have two words to the president: reform yourself."

Anne McBride, president of Common Cause, said Sunday the president should bear some responsibility for the fundraising mess. "The tone starts at the top," McBride said on Cable News Network's "Late Edition" program.

But McBride said the problem was widespread thoughout the American political system. "It's not simply a Democratic problem and not just a foreign problem," McBride said. "You also have huge amounts of money going to both parties, you have tobacco money."
